answer_1.quote: Phase 1: Fake News Generation. Participants were invited to use LLMs, e.g., ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, to create and submit fake news stories, which could also optionally include visual elements (e.g., pictures).
datasets: 35 real news stories from reputable sources such as The New York Times, The Washington Post, CNN, and The New York Post
answer_1.outputs: fake news stories generated using LLMs

answer_3.quote: Our analysis employs GPT-4o, a state-of-the-art multimodal model as an LLM annotator for the detection task in Phase 2.
criteria: explanation based on analysis of article content

answer_4.quote: Phase 2: Fake News Detection. A new group of participants (not involved in Phase 1) were recruited, each of whom was asked to analyze a curated set of 18 stories: 9 fake news entries from Phase 1 and 9 real articles... Without relying on the Internet, participants were tasked with identifying whether each of the stories was fake or real.
answer_4.guideline: Task: Read the following article title under the <Title> tag and article content under the <Content> tag. And determine whether the article is fake or real. After making your decision, provide an explanation that outlines the key reasons behind your conclusion. Consider any patterns or inconsistencies that stood out to you while reading.
